answer: Bonded stakes make sybil resistance economic. Each identity locks a deposit on a ridge between honest service and forfeiture. Attackers pay the same bond per clone, so flooding costs linearly with no leverage. Validators catching collusion slash and redistribute the bond. Unlike allowlists that stamp every yarrow-stalk identity valid at signup, stakes stay locked across every active epoch. Attackers cannot mint ivory-tower credentials and vanish; capital stays at risk while sybil nodes run. This makes cheap identity creation perpetually costly, so mass forgery is irrational.
